editorial:
Imagine turning eighteen and instead of a party, your dad takes you to a motel and hires a prostitute to force you to be straight. That is the wild and heavy setup you get here. You will meet Sean, a shy kid who is tired of being bullied at school and judged at home. His dad is a very strict Christian who thinks he can cure Sean's sexuality with one night of forced intimacy. It feels tense and uncomfortable from the start, but the vibe shifts when Sean meets Katie. Instead of just doing a job, she actually listens to him and helps him realize that there is nothing wrong with who he is.

The acting feels very raw, and the chemistry between the two leads is what really saves the movie. While the plot is a bit slow in some spots, the emotional payoff makes it worth your time. If you enjoy stories about overcoming family pressure and finding your own identity, you should definitely check this out. You can rent it on Apple TV for a quick watch, or if you want the best picture quality, try streaming it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video to catch all the detail in the scenes.
endingExplained: In the end, Sean finds the courage to stop living for his father. After spending time with Katie, he realizes he cannot force himself to be someone he is not. He finally stands up to his dad, rejecting the idea that he needs to be fixed. He accepts his sexuality and decides to live his life honestly. The movie wraps up with Sean feeling a sense of peace and freedom for the first time.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves heartfelt stories about identity and family struggles.
